_read_me: Thresholds and limits for the Jev Desk (guide Step 5). Edit on GitHub; the server picks up changes within ~15 minutes and logs which version every decision used. Entering needs a HIGHER bar than exiting: being wrong on an entry costs more than leaving early.

policy._enter_direction_conf: Jev must pick up or down with at least this confidence to open a position.
policy._enter_quality_min_level: What counts as a good entry: 0 Do not enter, 1 Marginal, 2 Good, 3 Excellent. 2 = 'Good or better'.
policy._enter_quality_p_good_min: Open a position only when Jev gives at least this chance that entry quality is Good or better. Changed 15 Oct from 'Good must be the top answer': in 312 decisions Jev's top answer was Good once, so nothing could trade. Replaying that day, 0.30 gave 14 signals (0.25 gave 39, 0.35 gave 6).
policy._enter_quality_conf: Not used while enter_quality_p_good_min is set.
policy._use_move_continues: Off since 15 Oct: Jev's 'move continues' read was backwards on our data (477 calls: when it said ~36%, moves continued 62% of the time; at ~53%, 46%). Still asked and tracked in the calibration report. If true, a new position needs at least enter_move_continues_min.
policy._use_jev_costs: Off: the spread is arithmetic, so code checks it (risk.max_spread_vs_normal) instead of Jev (guide Step 1: never spend a Jev call on arithmetic). The first day's log showed Jev reading normal spreads as abnormal. Jev is still asked, and its answer is logged for the calibration check. If true, no new position when Jev puts 'costs abnormal' at or above stand_aside_costs_abnormal.
policy._stand_aside_regimes: No new position when Jev is this sure the market is volatile (unpredictable) or quiet (moves too small to beat the spread).
policy._exit_urgency: Close a position when exit urgency reaches 'Close now' (3); move the stop closer at 'Tighten the stop' (2); both need this confidence.
policy._exit_on_opposite_direction_conf: Close a position when Jev points the other way with at least this confidence.

risk._risk_per_trade_pct: Position size is set so hitting the stop loses this % of equity.
risk._stop_and_target: Stop = this many 5-minute ATRs from entry. Target = stop distance x this multiple.
risk._max_same_usd_direction: All eight instruments move with the US dollar, so at most this many positions may bet the same way on the dollar.
risk._max_daily_loss_pct: Kill switch: lose this % of the day's starting equity and every position closes; no new trades until 00:00 UTC.
risk._max_drawdown_pct: Kill switch: fall this % below peak equity and every position closes; trading stays off until reset by hand (bash ~/paper-desk/server/reset-kill.sh).
risk._max_spread_vs_normal: No new position while the spread is wider than this multiple of its normal level (median of the last day). Checked by code.
risk._hold: Positions older than this are closed: Jev's direction call looks one hour ahead.
risk._friday: No new positions late on Friday, and everything is closed before the weekend gap.
risk._commission: Per lot, per side. The spread is already paid through the real bid/ask.
risk._max_leverage: Open positions' total size may not exceed this multiple of equity. A tight stop would otherwise mean a very large position; new positions are sized down to fit.

fallback._read_me: Guide Step 6, rung 4: when Jev is unavailable, simple rules written in code only. Plain trend-following with strict filters, at reduced size.
fallback._after_failed_rounds: Switch to the code-only rules after Jev has failed this many rounds in a row (one blip just holds).
fallback._risk_mult: Fallback trades risk this fraction of the normal risk per trade.
fallback._trend: Enter only when price is at least this many ATRs beyond the 20-bar EMA, the EMA is sloping that way, and price is on the same side of the 100-bar EMA.
fallback._rsi: ...and RSI is in this band: with the trend, but not stretched.
fallback._exit: Close when price crosses back over the 20-bar EMA, or RSI reaches these extremes.

vbo._read_me: Volume breakout: the main paper account since 23 Oct 2026. London breakout of the Asian range (00:00-07:00 UTC), first hourly close outside it between 07:00 and 11:00, only on high volume (RVOL), on the right side of VWAP, in a volatile market and with the daily trend. Validated in the Trading-Bot repo on 16 years of Octa hourly data. The values below are the selected (tested) variant: change them and the test no longer describes what is trading.
vbo._min_rvol: The breakout bar's tick volume must be at least this multiple of that hour's 20-day average.
vbo._sl_cap_atr: Stop = far side of the Asian range, but never more than this many hourly ATRs away.
vbo._limits: Same limits as the validation: 0.5% risk per trade, 3 open positions, stop for the day after a 2% loss or 4 losses in a row, one trade per instrument per day.
vbo._max_drawdown_pct: Kill switch: this account stops (until reset-kill.sh) if it falls this far below its peak. The test's worst drawdown was 3.5%.
vbo._windows: Asian range 00:00-07:00 UTC, London entry 07:00-11:00 UTC. Only these windows were validated.
vbo._exit_utc_hour: Every position is closed at this UTC hour (as in the test).
vbo._news_window_min: No new position this many minutes either side of a listed high-impact release (config/news_blackout.csv).

vbo_ny._read_me: NY breakout: London range (07:00-13:00 UTC) → entry 13:00-18:00 UTC = 18:30-23:30 Dubai. Uses the SAME code as the London breakout, just different windows. NOT individually validated on real MT5 data — judge it over a few months and set enabled=false if it loses. 10% drawdown kill switch stops it on its own if it goes badly.

vbo_asia._read_me: Asia breakout: NY range (13:00-20:00 UTC) → entry 20:00-23:00 UTC = 01:30-04:30 Dubai, feeding into the Asia session. Uses the SAME code as the London breakout, just different windows. NOT individually validated on real MT5 data — judge it over a few months and set enabled=false if it loses. This is the most experimental of the three.

alerts._read_me: Telegram messages to your phone (set up with: bash ~/paper-desk/server/telegram.sh). Rung 5 of the ladder: kill switch -> send yourself an alert.
alerts._bridge_down_min: Alert when the MT5 bridge has sent nothing for this many minutes while the market is open.
alerts._daily_summary_utc: A short daily report after the New York close.
